'''Moroff''' was a [[Gigoran]] [[Gender|male]] [[mercenary]] who was active during the [[Imperial Era]]. As a towering [[gunner]], he sought out combat zones across [[the galaxy]] with the goal of selling his services to anyone who required it. Moroff eventually joined the [[Partisans]], a militia group led by the resistance fighter [[Saw Gerrera]], and [[Campaigns of Saw Gerrera's Partisans|fought]] against the [[Galactic Empire]] in the hope of making a [[Currency|profit]]. During his [[time]] with the group, Moroff was present at the Partisans' [[Resistance base|base]] on the [[planet]] [[D'Qar]] and also participated in a [[rhydonium]] [[Rhydonium heist|raid]] on a [[Unidentified planet (Rhydonium heist)|planet]]. Around [[1 BBY]], he was part of [[Assault on Dooma 4|mission]] on the astronomical object [[Dooma 4]], ending in the destruction of the [[Imperial Metal Factory]]. At some point by 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], Moroff had a [[bounty]] placed on his head by the Empire, and he was present at [[Gesh's Tapcafe]] in [[Jedha City]] on the [[moon]] of [[Jedha]] but fled when an [[Unidentified Imperial spy (Jedha)|Imperial spy]] reported his presence to a [[stormtrooper]] patrol.

In 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], Moroff was on Jedha during the Partisans' [[Jedha insurgency|skirmishes]] against [[Imperial Military|Imperial forces]] in the area. He was among the group of Partisans who captured and brought the defecting Imperial [[pilot]] [[Bodhi Rook]] before Gerrera in their hideout located in the [[Catacombs of Cadera]]. They later took part in a [[Battle on Jedha|battle]] against a local Imperial [[Imperial Hammers Elite Armor Unit|patrol]] in Jedha City, resulting in the group stealing a shipment of [[kyber crystal]]s that the Imperials possessed. Shortly after, Moroff was present in the Catacombs when Jedha City was [[Destruction of Jedha City|destroyed]] by the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]], resulting in the [[death]] of Gerrera and many Partisans.

==Biography==
===Joining the Partisans===
{{Quote|And ''Chamdaka'', brother of Moroff of Gigor.|M.A.R. Corps member Blades, to the Sith [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="Vader 49" />}}
[[File:Partisans.svg|thumb|right|250px|Moroff joined the Partisans (logo pictured).]]
[[Homeworld|Hailing]] from<ref name="Vader 49" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]]<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion">''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]''</ref> [[Gigor]],<ref name="Vader 49" /> the [[Gigoran]] [[Gender|male]]<ref name="Moroff DB" /> Moroff had a Gigoran brother named [[Chamdaka]]<ref name="Vader 49" /> and operated as a [[mercenary]] during the [[Imperial Era]]. Realizing the potential [[Currency|money]] to be made as a [[gunner]], he traveled around [[the galaxy]] in order to seek out combat zones, aiming to sell his brawn and firepower to anyone who would require them.<ref name="Visual Guide" /> He later became an outlaw when he joined the [[Partisans]],<ref name="Alien Archive">''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]''</ref> an extremist militia group led by the resistance fighter [[Saw Gerrera]],<ref name="Visual Guide" /> and [[Campaigns of Saw Gerrera's Partisans|fought]] against the [[Galactic Empire]] in order to generate profit,<ref name="Absolutely">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> which he managed to acquire at a substantial rate.<ref name="Finest-2019">{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Finest Star Wars|subset=''Rogue One''|cardname=Moroff|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/192570/cid/12174320}}</ref>

Moroff was later listed as a known associate of Gerrera on wanted posters created by the Empire, alongside fellow Partisans [[Beezer Fortuna]], [[Weeteef Cyu-Bee]],<ref name="RebelFiles">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref><ref name="SaV">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref> and the [[Tognath]] [[eggmate]]s<ref name="Visual Guide" /> [[Edrio]] and [[Benthic]].<ref name="RebelFiles" /><ref name="SaV" /> One of the posters was included in a compilation of documents known as ''[[The Rebel Files]]'' in a section titled "[[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Alliance]] Chron 1"<ref name="RebelFiles" /> that spanned approximately between [[5 BBY]] and [[2 BBY]].<ref name="Rebel Files date">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' states that ''[[The Rebel Files]]''{{'}} "[[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Alliance]] Chron 1" section, which mentions the ''Unassailable'', spans 14–17 [[Imperial calendar|AFE]], or fourteen to seventeen [[Standard year|years]] after the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[19 BBY]]. Therefore, those dates equate to between [[5 BBY]] and [[2 BBY]].</ref> Another was included in a file dated to [[6 BBY|7971]] [[Coruscant reckoning calendar|C.R.C.]] in ''[[Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]'', a collection of case files compiled by the head of the planet [[Hosnian Prime]]'s [[Law enforcement agency|law enforcement]], [[Commissioner]] [[Exantor Divo]],<ref name="SaV" /> in [[34 ABY]].<ref name="ScumAndVillainyDate">{{ScumAndVillainyDate}}</ref>

===Action with the Partisans===
{{Quote|Stand your ground! We're going to be here for a while!|Saw Gerrera gives an order to Moroff and the Partisans on Dooma 4|<ref name="Rebels-Mag4">{{RebelsAnimationCite|4|Crossing the Line}}</ref>}}
In 5 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]],<ref name="Narkina Trivia">{{AndorDate|108}}</ref> Moroff and the Partisans were stationed at a [[Saw Gerrera's Base|base]] on<ref name="Narkina 5">{{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}}</ref> the planet<ref name="Narkina 5 AD">{{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}} {{AD|Disney+}}</ref> [[Segra Milo]]. The Gigoran stood at an open area of the base while the rebel [[Luthen Rael]] spoke with Gerrera inside, offering the Partisans a mission to assist rebel [[Anto Kreegyr]]. He refused to risk the lives of his forces for the attack, dismissing Kreegyr as a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]].<ref name="Narkina 5" /> Later on, however, Gerrera was willing to take on the mission. When Rael visited again, Moroff was patrolling the base. The rebel advised Gerrera not to assist Kreegyr in order to safeguard their rebellion against the Empire, as the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] had laid a trap for Kreegyr and his [[Anto Kreegyr's group|men]]. After a heated confrontation, Gerrera agreed to avoid meeting him.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix">{{Andor|Daughter of Ferrix}}</ref>

[[3 BBY|Two years later]], Moroff was stationed on<ref name="Ghorman">{{Andor|Ever Been to Ghorman?}}</ref> the planet<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref> [[D'Qar]]. During that time, the operative [[Wilmon Paak]] was sent to the Partisans to teach a [[rhydonium]]-generating technique. When Gererra called a meeting, Moroff walked inside the [[Resistance base|base]]. Gerrera told the assembled, Moroff included, to imagine what Paak's machine could do for them: if they ever needed rhydonium, they could find a vein and use Paak's machine and inhale the addictive, high-inducing substance. When Gererra brought forward the Partisan [[Pluti]] to be Paak's student, Moroff moved to the side to make way for the former to come through the crowd.<ref name="Ghorman" /> Not long afterward, the Partisan leader exposed Pluti as a traitor, announcing they would be packing up soon and embarking on a rhydonium [[Rhydonium heist|raid]]. Moroff and the other Partisans cheered at the news. He further instructed the group to burn whatever they did not take with them. Afterward, the group, including Moroff, went to a [[Unidentified planet (Rhydonium heist)|planet]] and successfully raided rhydonium from a pipeline there. Moroff watched from above as Pak used a device to steal the rhydonium, with Gererra addressing the triumph in range of those present after the job was complete.<ref name="IHaveFriends">{{Andor|I Have Friends Everywhere}}</ref>

[[File:Partisans-Dooma4-RebelsMagazine4.png|thumb|left|300px|Moroff and the Partisans assault the Imperial Metal Factory on Dooma 4.]]
Around [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Crossing the Line date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of "[[Crossing the Line]]" to around [[1 BBY]].</ref> Moroff and the Partisans, led by Gerrera and [[Lieutenant]] [[Megyn Soone]], [[Assault on Dooma 4|attacked]] the [[Imperial Metal Factory]] on the astronomical object [[Dooma 4]]. After rushing to the entrance, the group took cover behind various crates. Despite being heavily outgunned, they held their ground on Gerrera's orders when Soone left their position to plant [[Bomb|explosives]] within the [[factory]]. She was captured, however, and Gerrera entered the factory to rescue her and [[Detonator|detonate]] the explosives himself. Moroff and the others retreated to their [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-wing]] soon after on the orders of Edrio, who was [[pilot]]ing the [[Starship|ship]]. They reunited with Gerrera and Soone aboard the ship after the explosives were detonated and departed the factory.<ref name="Rebels-Mag4" />

===Jedha===
{{Quote|What part of 'urgent message' do you guys not understand? We are all on the same side. If you see past the uniform for a minute.|audio=BodhiRook-Message.flac|Bodhi Rook attempts to communicate with his captors, including Moroff|<ref name="Rogue One">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>}}
[[File:RookGunpoint-RogueOne1.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Moroff (second from left) and the Partisans hold Bodhi Rook at gunpoint.]]
At some point, the Partisans relocated their base of operations to the [[Catacombs of Cadera]] located on the [[desert]] [[moon]] of [[Jedha]], where they [[Jedha insurgency|clashed]] with the local [[Imperial Military|Imperials]] on several occasions.<ref name="Visual Guide" /> At one point by 1 BBY,<ref name="Date">The scenario "Secret Mission on Jedha" of ''[[Unlock!: Star Wars Escape Game]]'' is set before the [[destruction of Jedha City]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[1 BBY]].</ref> Moroff was deemed a dangerous enough criminal by the Empire to have a [[bounty]] placed on him. A photograph of him was displayed alongside photographs of other criminals and offenders on a [[Viewscreen|holoscreen]] near the entrance of [[Gesh's Tapcafe]] in [[Jedha City]]. He was present at the [[tapcafe]] when an [[Unidentified Imperial spy (Jedha)|Imperial spy]] entered the establishment, upon which the Gigoran glared when the [[spy]] passed by him. They then reported Moroff's presence to a [[stormtrooper]] patrol, causing him to flee as soon as he saw them. The patrol fired upon him while he made his escape. As a result of Moroff's departure, the patrons of the tapcafe became more relaxed.<ref name="Unlock">''[[Unlock!: Star Wars Escape Game]]''</ref> In 1 BBY,<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events on [[Jedha]] in ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', which includes Moroff's appearance, to [[1 BBY]].</ref> Moroff was patrolling the desert<ref name="Birth of the Rebellion">{{EncyclopediaCite|The Birth of the Rebellion}}</ref> and was among a group of Partisans when [[Bodhi Rook]], a pilot who defected from the Empire, appeared before them. They quickly trained their [[weapon]]s at him as they believed he was an Imperial. After Rook informed them of his defection and that he had a message for Gerrera, the group captured the pilot.<ref name="RO-Comic1">[[Rogue One Adaptation 1|''Rogue One Adaptation'' 1]]</ref>

Moroff and the group brought the pilot before Benthic and another group of Partisans. Benthic [[Torture|interrogated]] him briefly before ordering the others to place a bag over the pilot's head and take him to Gerrera for further questioning.<ref name="Rogue One" /> As the term "defector" had no translation in the [[Tognath (language)|Tognath language]], Moroff defined the concept to Benthic, who would have [[Death|killed]] the pilot had he not been informed about Rook's defection. The explanation allowed the pilot to survive his encounter with the Partisans.<ref name="Visual Guide" />

[[File:Jedha_insurgency.png|thumb|left|300px|Moroff (left) and the Partisans escape right after Imperial forces arrive.]]
Moroff later participated in a [[Battle on Jedha|raid]] against the [[Imperial Hammers Elite Armor Unit]], which included a [[TX-225 GAVw "Occupier" combat assault tank|TX-225 combat assault tank]] carrying a [[Kyber crystal container|shipment]] of [[kyber crystal]]s, in [[Tythoni Square]] within Jedha City.<ref name="Rogue One" /> The Gigoran was in charge of taking out containers of [[crystal]]s from the battlefield.<ref name="Birth of the Rebellion" /> After the Imperial unit was eliminated, the Gigoran and the Partisans quickly looted the [[tank]] and acquired the kyber, placing the crystals within containers of their own. As an [[All Terrain Scout Transport|AT-ST]] [[walker]] and more Imperials arrived, Moroff and the others quickly fled into an alleyway with the containers in [[Limb|hand]].<ref name="Rogue One" /> After the battle, he was present at the Catacombs when the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] [[Destruction of Jedha City|obliterated]] Jedha City, causing a massive shockwave.<ref name="RO-Comic3">[[Rogue One Adaptation 3|''Rogue One Adaptation'' 3]]</ref> The Partisans quickly evacuated their base, although Gerrera stayed behind and perished when the structure collapsed in the shockwave.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Numerous Partisans also lost their lives in the event,<ref name="Inferno Squad">''[[Battlefront II: Inferno Squad]]''</ref> although it was unknown whether or not Moroff survived.<ref name="Chewbacca Encyclopedia">{{EncyclopediaCite|Chewbacca and Other Aliens of the Rebellion and the Resistance}}</ref>

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Perhaps the most famed of this usually peaceful species is Moroff, a Gigoran mercenary who sells his skills to the highest bidder, regardless of political allegiance.|A description of Moroff in a restored journal entry on Gigorans|<ref name="Alien Archive" />}}
Moroff and his [[species]] were detailed in an [[Unidentified artist|artist's]] [[Unidentified artist's journal|journal]], which described the mercenary as the most famous member of the Gigorans, who were normally peaceful individuals. The document was later restored, expanded, and kept in the [[Graf Archive]]<ref name="Alien Archive" /> at some point no earlier than 34 ABY.<ref name="Year">{{AlienArchiveJournalDate}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Moroff-DB.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Moroff enjoyed being a gunner.]]
Moroff had [[Color|white]] [[Hair|fur]] and black [[eye]]s. Tall and brawny, he believed there was money to be made as a heavy gunner and was disinterested in the ongoing [[Galactic Civil War|conflict]] between the Rebel Alliance and the Empire.<ref name="Visual Guide" /> Motivated by nothing more than greed,<ref name="Chewbacca Encyclopedia" /> he sold his skills to the highest bidder, disregarding their political allegiance,<ref name="Alien Archive" /> and found like-minded individuals when he joined the Partisans.<ref name="Visual Guide" /> Despite claims of being apolitical, the mercenary displayed strong loyalty to Saw Gerrera, even when pickings were slim.<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion Visual Guide">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref>

Moroff was usually grumpy and performed tasks begrudgingly when asked to do so. However, his rude replies in his [[Gigoran (language)|native language]] were always translated by his [[Translating vocoder|voice-translator box]] into pleasant and cheerful responses in [[Galactic Basic Standard]],<ref name="RO-Magazine">''[[Entertainment Weekly's Ultimate Guide to Rogue One]]''</ref> a [[language]] he was normally unable to speak. He enjoyed his role as a towering gunner, carrying his [[Vulk TAU-6-23 "Blastmill" rotary blaster cannon|blaster cannon]] as if it weighed nothing at all.<ref name="HC-40">{{HelmetCollectionCite|40|Databank A-Z}}</ref> When an Imperial spy passed by him at Gesh's Tapcafe, Moroff glared at the spy and was unimpressed with them. To the spy, Moroff appeared seedy-looking and rough around the edges.<ref name="Unlock" />

==Equipment==
In order to establish vital communication with his fellow Partisans during combat,<ref name="HC-40" /> Moroff wore a [[vocoder mask]] on his [[mouth]],<ref name="Visual Guide" /> translating his speech into Basic for his comrades to understand.<ref name="HC-40" /> He also carried a large [[backpack]] and wore multiple equipment pouches around his waist.<ref name="Visual Guide" /> During the mission on Dooma 4, he engaged Imperial forces with a ranged weapon.<ref name="Rebels-Mag4" /> While operating on Jedha, Moroff was armed with a Vulk TAU-6-23 "Blastmill" rotary [[blaster cannon]],<ref name="Visual Guide" /> his favorite model of heavy [[blaster]] [[cannon]].<ref name="Chewbacca Encyclopedia" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Appearance and portrayal===
{{Quote|Moroff is a bit disgruntled about his life but would never cross the line. So Ian Whyte, who plays him, used that as an understanding of how Moroff might move.|Neal Scanlan|<ref name="Debrief">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story - The Official Mission Debrief]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Moroff-R1-Set.png|thumb|left|300px|Ian Whyte as Moroff on ''Rogue One''{{'s}} Scarif set]]
Moroff first appeared in the [[Gareth Edwards]]-directed [[Star Wars Anthology Series|anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref name="Rogue One" /> released on [[December 16]], [[2016]].<ref name="Director Announced">{{SW|url=news/gareth-edwards-and-gary-whitta-onboard-for-star-wars-stand-alone-film|text=Gareth Edwards and Gary Whitta Onboard for ''Star Wars'' Stand-Alone Film}}</ref> The character was portrayed by [[Ian Whyte]], who previously played [[Roodown]] and [[Bollie Prindel]] in the [[2015]] [[sequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']].<ref name="Moroff-Actor">{{WebCite|url=https://www.spotlight.com/0617-7831-1959|text=Spotlight: Ian Whyte|work=[[Wikipedia:Spotlight (company|Spotlight]]|archivedate=20200214103105}}</ref> Prior to the film's release, the character was first pictured in a behind-the-scenes video released on [[July 15]], 2016.<ref name="Celebration Reel">{{SWYouTube|HUb_zpdyDpU|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story - Celebration Reel|sw_url=video/rogue-one-a-star-wars-story-celebration-reel}}</ref> He was then named in a toy released as part of the [[Star Wars: Rogue One (toy line)|''Star Wars: Rogue One'' toy line]] by [[Hasbro]]<ref name="Moroff-Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Rogue One (toy line)|pack=Scarif Stormtrooper & Moroff Deluxe Pack|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/Moroff-VS-Scarif-Stormtrooper-Squad-Leader-Rogue-One.asp}}</ref> on [[September 29]], 2016.<ref name="Moroff-Hasbro-Amazon">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Scarif-Stormtrooper-Moroff/dp/B01BY1K8H8|text=Star Wars Rogue One Scarif Stormtrooper & Moroff Deluxe Pack}}</ref>

During ''Rogue One''{{'s}} production, Moroff was codenamed "G030," and Whyte was photographed wearing the costume from every possible angle in order to preserve material for future special effects and products.<ref name="Visual Guide" /> While some pre-release footage from the film shows Moroff participating in the [[Battle of Scarif]],<ref name="RO-Creature">{{SWYouTube|P2N0Mn4i4Dw|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story "Creature Featurette"|sw_url=video/rogue-one-a-star-wars-story-creature-featurette}}</ref> he is not seen in any [[Scarif]] scenes in the final cut of the movie.<ref name="Rogue One" /> The Jedha desert scenes were filmed at [[Wikipedia:Wadi Rum|Wadi Rum]], [[Wikipedia:Jordan|Jordan]] in 2015<ref name="Jordan Times">{{WebCite|url=http://www.jordantimes.com/news/local/rfc-bags-outstanding-film-commission%E2%80%99-award|text=RFC bags 'Outstanding Film Commission' Award|date=2017-04-10|work=[[Wikipedia:The Jordan Times|The Jordan Times]]|quote=The RFC earned this award for the American science fiction film "Rogue One: A Star Wars Story", directed by Gareth Edwards, that was shot in Wadi Rum in 2015, the statement said.|archivedate=20191015052241}}</ref> while the Jedha City scenes were filmed at [[Pinewood Studios]] in [[Wikipedia:Slough|Slough]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]].<ref name="Locations Featurette">{{SWYouTube|yzY8Mi4G04g|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story "Locations" Featurette|sw_url=video/rogue-one-a-star-wars-story-locations-featurette}}</ref>

===Conception and design===
{{Quote|There haven't been many versions of big, furry characters other than Chewbacca, and so we thought what can we introduce that would live alongside a Wookiee?|Neal Scanlan|<ref name="Debrief" />}}
[[File:Senna_Rogue_One.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An early piece of concept art for Senna, the character that ultimately became the Gigoran Moroff]]
Special effects artist [[Neal Scanlan]] stated that Moroff's character was born from the idea that ''Rogue One'' could feature a tall, furry individual reminiscent of the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]]. Edwards found the idea of a new species whose size and strength were taken advantage of appealing, and the Gigoran species was chosen for the film.<ref name="Debrief" /> To decide on Moroff's species, [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] took inspiration from<ref name="Moroff Hidalgo">{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-talking-rogue-one-aliens-with-pablo-hidalgo|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: Talking ''Rogue One'' Aliens with Pablo Hidalgo}}</ref> a [[Gigoran/Legends|Gigoran]] named [[Rollos]] in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity who was featured in the [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying game]] article "[[It's a Gambler's Life]]," written by [[Tony Russo|Anthony P. Russo]] and published in the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 4|fourth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine in [[February]] [[1994]].<ref name="Gambler">{{JournalCite|4|It's a Gambler's Life}}</ref>

According to Scanlan, Moroff refrained from "crossing the line" and was "disgruntled about his life," further adding that the character was lethargic and wished to stop fighting, but the Gigoran was there to support as he was a "good guy." Whyte used the character's personality as the basis for understanding Moroff's physical movement.<ref name="Debrief" /> The effects team and Edwards would joke that a Wookiee and a [[wampa]] encountered each other and "had a romantic interlude," resulting in the Gigoran's creation.<ref name="Which Alien">{{StarWarsShow|kSSPQEAL8w0|Which Rogue One Alien Wears an iPhone and a Major Marvel Star Wars Comics Crossover Revealed|sw_url=video/the-star-wars-show-episode-36}}</ref>

The character that became Moroff was originally a rebel named Senna,<ref name="Visual Guide" /> who was one of several characters conceived to be a part of the [[Rogue One]] team seen in the film, alongside characters [[Lunak]], [[Dray Nevis]], [[Sabine Wren|Ria Talla]], and [[Jerris Kestal]]. He was intended to be a duo with the character of Lunak. Concept art for the character was created by artists [[Christian Alzmann]], [[Tyler Scarlet]], [[Karla Ortiz]], [[Luke Fisher]], [[Ivan Manzella]], and [[Karl Lindberg]]. Alzmann imagined Senna to be a tall figure akin to Chewbacca,<ref name="RO-Art">''[[The Art of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> a thought shared by Scanlan and the film's production team.<ref name="Debrief" />

[[File:Moroff-IvanManzella.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Moroff artwork by Ivan Manzella]]
Senna's character underwent several designs, including a nearly [[Unidentified large-armed species|hairless brute]], a large [[Reptile|reptilian]]-like character, an elf-like character with a blaster rifle, a character with a [[wolf]]-like appearance, and finally the Gigoran<ref name="RO-Art" /> that was ultimately renamed Moroff and given a much smaller role in the film.<ref name="Visual Guide" /> The character, however, was consistently drawn as an [[alien]] male.<ref name="RO-Art" /> The name "Senna" would later be used for another [[Senna (Gigoran)|Gigoran character]] featured in the [[2018]] anthology film, ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="Solo-Guide">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''</ref>

===Costume and ''Andor''===
{{Quote|It fits him like his skin, so as Ian moves, the muscles move, and the fur suit does the same.|Neal Scanlan|<ref name="Magic">''[[The Moviemaking Magic of Star Wars: Creatures & Aliens]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Whyte-Costume.png|thumb|right|300px|Ian Whyte in Moroff's costume]]
The character's costume was created from fabric and foam and was covered in knotted hair to emulate the white fur. Ian Whyte wore a skull cap, upon which Moroff's animatronic head was placed. In order to connect the head with the rest of the body, a zip was created around the neckline and the back of the costume. To get into the costume, Whyte first entered the body wearing the skull cap, followed by the production team placing the head over the cap.<ref name="Magic" />

To finish the process, the costume was zipped up to join the head and the body together. The costume also included large "wampa-like" feet made of rubber in order to make Whyte look taller, as well as a pair of gloves. Moroff's facial expressions were controlled by an operator off-camera using radio control. In total, the costume stood at a height of seven feet and seven inches.<ref name="Magic" /> The costume's chest piece contained an [[Wikipedia:iPhone|iPhone]] that displayed the soundwaves of the operator's voice.<ref name="Which Alien" />

This design was very similar to the process used for creating Wookiees, with both costumes using minimal animatronics, although Moroff's head was higher than that of a Wookiee character like Chewbacca. Both Scanlan and [[Tony Gilroy]], director of ''Rogue One'', loved Moroff's design and, as Gilroy felt that the character's presence was right for his new series [[Star Wars: Andor|''Andor'']], the Gigoran was brought forward to appear in the show.<ref name="B&A">{{BookCite|author=Failes, Ian|title=befores & aftersnumber=#33|date=2025-06-17|pages=60|isbn=979-8287898458|link=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FDKBM53C}}</ref>

===LEGO content===
[[File:Moroff-Raddus-X-wingChallenge.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=Moroff stands with his arms behind his back beside Raddus who is looking at a holoprojector table in a hangar in the Great Temple on Yavin 4. In the background, a pair of parked U-wings are visible.|Moroff appeared with Admiral Raddus in several LEGO shorts on YouTube.]]
In the non-canon comic strip "[[Operation: Bunker Bust!]]," published in the [[January]]-February [[2017]] issue of the [[LEGO Magazine|''LEGO Club Magazine'']], Moroff stands beside [[Admiral]] [[Raddus]] of the Rebel Alliance in a [[hangar]] of the [[Great Temple]] rebel headquarters on the moon [[Yavin 4]] as they see off a [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber]], which had been loaded by a [[rebel pilot]] and [[R3-S1]] to join the Battle of Scarif.<ref name="Bunker Bust">{{LegoMagazineCite|club=1|issue=January/February 2017|story=Operation: Bunker Bust!}}</ref> Moroff also appeared in two animated videos posted to the official [[LEGO]] [[Wikipedia:YouTube|YouTube]] channel. In the first, he is stood outside the Yavin 4 Great Temple with Raddus with a pair of [[binoculars]].<ref name="Green Squadron">{{LegoMiniMovie|IyTV39IbcdA|A-wing Challenge}}</ref> In the second, he is stood with Raddus at a console inside the temple.<ref name="Red Squadron">{{LegoMiniMovie|TLNL-H4NsY4|X-wing Challenge}}</ref>

Moroff appears in the non-[[canon]] [[2021]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars Battles]]'' as an unlockable "[[Light side of the Force|light side]]" unit. The game describes him as a cousin of [[Lessof]].<ref name="LSWB">''[[LEGO Star Wars Battles]]''</ref> Moroff was one of the characters featured in the non-canon browser game [[LEGO Kids Memory Game]] released on LEGO.com, released the same year.<ref name="LEGOPAIRS">{{LEGOWeb|url=en-us/kids/star-wars/find-the-pairs|text=Find the pairs|nolive=1}}</ref>
